title: Copperfold education assistant pilot notes
content:
Meeting: Copperfold (K12 LMS provider) technical kickoff
Date: 2024-10-14 call (notes captured by Leah)
Attendees: Leah (Redwood SE), Maya (Redwood PM), Arun (Redwood infra), Kate M. (Copperfold eng lead), J. Alvarez (Copperfold product), Legal rep: S. Roe (brief intro)

1) Goals / ask from Copperfold
- Build a teacher-assistant flow: auto-summarize submitted student handwritten assignments (images + short voice notes) and produce feedback bullets + rubric alignment.
- Target pilot: 200 classrooms, ~5k students, peak concurrency 150 simultaneous inference requests during grading windows.
- Hard constraint: FERPA compliance (no student data stored outside VPC).
- Low-latency expectation for UI: 1–2s for text-only chat; up to 4–6s acceptable for image-to-feedback since OCR + multimodal pipeline involved.

2) Architecture ideas we sketched on call
- Client (browser/mobile) uploads image -> Copperfold backend (on-prem or cloud) -> Redwood Private deployed in their staging VPC (customer-managed).
- Pipeline: OCR (Tesseract or Vision API placeholder) -> preproc -> Redwood endpoint for: a) embedding retrieval (class rubrics, prior examples) and b) generation for feedback.
- Option: run OCR in-house and send pre-extracted text + image hash to Redwood to avoid sending raw student images. We proposed a KMS policy and ephemeral token scheme.

3) Requirements (explicit / non-negotiable)
- Data residency: models and inference must run in their VPC; no tokens/cleartext student PII allowed in hosted logs.
- Audit logs for every inference (timestamp, model id, route id, request size) retained for 1 year.
- TLS + client cert auth for server-to-server traffic + SCIM SSO integration (Okta).
- Support model pinning and canary rollouts for pilot so they can validate quality changes before fleet-wide rollout.

4) Capacity & cost roughing (quick calc on call)
- Average combined request size after OCR: ~1.2k tokens.
- If using a 70B open model quantized to 4-bit dedicated, estimate ~3.5–4 RPS per GPU for 1.2k tokens under current kernel profile. For peak 150 concurrent sustained requests we recommended reserved Dedicated pool with autoscale + burst.
- Preliminary cost window: $8–12k/month for pilot depending on model choice and GPU type (A10 vs A100). We'll formalize after exact model/sequence length distribution.

5) Quality & model considerations
- Students handwriting quality varies a lot—OCR errors drive hallucinations. Strong preference to keep original image hash metadata and top-3 OCR candidates; pass candidates into generation as explicit evidence.
- Use retrieval-augmented generation with small in-memory index of class-specific rubrics. Avoid global nearest-neighbor index with student PII.
- Suggest evaluation set: 200 hand-annotated examples (teacher-provided) to measure feedback precision/recall and rubric alignment.

6) Gotchas / red flags we flagged live
- FERPA + vendor addendum: Copperfold legal needs explicit assurance we can operate under their DPA + custom FERPA terms. Likely requires private control plane and no hosted logs.
- OCR latency/spikiness could break UI expectations. Need distributed OCR workers or client-side pre-scan option.
- Tokenization mismatch: some handwritten math/characters produce long token sequences; must cap and normalize (strip image-extracted artifacts).
- Embedding drift: if teachers edit rubrics, cached embeddings must invalidate quickly or we risk stale feedback.

7) Security / compliance items to confirm
- KMS integration: customer-managed key (BYOK) required for pilot.
- HSM for production? They asked about HSM but for pilot BYOK/KMS acceptable.
- SOC2 + data processing addendum + support for audit snapshots in console.

8) Open questions (needs answers before next sync)
- Kate: will Copperfold run OCR entirely in their environment or allow image forwarding to Redwood? (Action: Kate to confirm by 2024-10-21)
- Legal: are there any state-specific student data rules (CA CCPA-ish) we must handle differently?
- Ops: what SLA for labeling corrections? If teacher rejects feedback, who retrains / updates retrieval docs?

9) Immediate next steps / owners
- Leah: follow up with solution diagram + VPC network flow diagram (due 2024-10-18).
- Arun: rough Dedicated sizing options (A10 vs A100) + cost table for 3 scenarios by 2024-10-20.
- Maya: draft DPA addendum template and example KMS + audit log retention language by 2024-10-25.
- Kate (Copperfold): confirm OCR plan and share anonymized sample set (200 examples) by 2024-10-21.

10) Suggested pilot success metrics (we proposed)
- NPS from teachers on generated feedback >= 70 after 6 weeks.
- Feedback precision: >= 85% (measured against teacher-labeled gold set).
- Average end-to-end latency (UI) <= 4s for image->feedback for 90th percentile.
- Operational: < 1% failure rate and ability to rollback model within 5 minutes.

11) Notes to self / friction points for Redwood sales/eng alignment
- Need clear private-deploy onboarding runbook (network peering, egress policy, cert handoff) for non-core infra teams at customers.
- Prep a calm-fallback model (smaller LLM) that runs cheaper and has deterministic behavior for classroom-critical windows (grading deadlines).
- Pre-bake a rubric ingestion pipeline that outputs sanitized docs + embeddings and handles versioning.

Unresolved / parking-lot items:
- Cost split for OCR if Copperfold opts to use Redwood-managed OCR (they seemed hesitant).
- Data retention policy details for student audio clips (voice notes) -- automatic deletion policy needed.

Quick links / refs mentioned in call:
- EDU-1293 (pilot intake ticket)
- Confluence: copperfold/edu-assistant-pilot (planning page)
- Slack thread: #pilot-copperfold (link posted by Kate)

Timestamped action owner summary:
- Leah: solution diagram + network flow (2024-10-18)
- Arun: dedicated sizing + cost scenarios (2024-10-20)
- Maya: DPA/KMS wording draft (2024-10-25)
- Kate: OCR confirmation + sample set (2024-10-21)

----
Notes: keep this doc informal. Will convert to a more formal pilot brief once Kate confirms OCR path and legal approves DPA addendum.

End of notes.
